engines: Google AI Overviews and Perplexity, across the All Over Ointment and a sample of the catalog
lead: Here is the riskiest thing AI tells parents about Tubby Todd today. When a parent asks whether the All Over Ointment is fragrance-free, Perplexity says yes and never mentions the Lavender Rosemary scented version, so a fragrance-reactive baby could end up with a scented product. That is the one safety-relevant gap, and it is fixable. Across the rest of the catalog the hard facts mostly hold up. Google states your active ingredients correctly, including the All Over Ointment, Bye-Bye Cradle Cap, and Sweet Cheeks Diaper Paste, and it gets your lotion scents right. The gaps that remain are on Perplexity and in how AI frames your products, and this report covers each one with the fix.

score.note: Tubby Todd is a strong performer. Google AI Overviews states the hard facts correctly across the products we checked. The lost points come from Perplexity omitting the scented version, both engines understating the All Over Ointment as a moisturizer rather than the OTC eczema treatment it is, and Tubby Todd being left off best for newborns lists.

areas.note: Hard specs and active ingredients are correct across the products we checked

findings.query: is the All Over Ointment fragrance-free? (Perplexity)
findings.wrong: that the ointment is fragrance-free, with a second fragrance-free version for sensitive skin
findings.truth: Tubby Todd makes a Lavender Rosemary scented version of the All Over Ointment, which Perplexity never mentions.
findings.impact: A parent with a fragrance-reactive or eczema-prone baby could buy the scented version assuming it has no fragrance.

findings.query: is it a real eczema treatment? (Perplexity, and Google's eczema overview)
findings.wrong: that it is not a medication and not a medical treatment, better seen as supportive moisturizing care
findings.verdict: That understates it, and AI is inconsistent about it.
findings.truth: The All Over Ointment is an FDA over-the-counter eczema treatment with 1% colloidal oatmeal as the active ingredient and the National Eczema Association seal. Asked directly, Google states this correctly, so the framing depends on how the question is phrased.
findings.impact: When AI hedges on whether it is a real treatment, parents lean toward products AI labels as treatments.

findings.query: best baby eczema cream for newborns (Google AI Overviews)
findings.wrong: with Aveeno, Mustela, and Eucerin named and Tubby Todd left off the list
findings.verdict: That omits a product that qualifies.
findings.truth: Tubby Todd is newborn-safe, uses the same colloidal oatmeal active, and carries the National Eczema Association seal, so it fits the list AI built.
findings.impact: You are invisible at the exact moment a parent asks AI what to buy.

findings.query: hard specs across the catalog (Google AI Overviews)
findings.wrong: the All Over Ointment at 1% colloidal oatmeal, Bye-Bye Cradle Cap at 0.95% pyrithione zinc, Sweet Cheeks Diaper Paste at 14% zinc oxide, and the Everyday Lotion scents
findings.truth: Every one of these matches Tubby Todd's own product pages, including the two over-the-counter drug actives.
findings.impact: This is what AI gets right, so the job is to keep it accurate as your catalog changes and to fix the gaps above.
